field_name: A potentially self-injurious act committed with at least some wish to die, as a result of act. Behaviour was in part thought of as method to kill oneself. Intent does not have to be 100%. If there is any intent/desire to die associated with the act, then it can be considered an actual suicide attempt. There does not have to be any injury or harm, just the potential for injury or harm. If person pulls trigger while gun is in mouth but gun is broken so no injury results, this is considered an attempt. Inferring Intent: Even if an individual denies intent/wish to die, it may be inferred clinically from the behaviour or circumstances. For example, a highly lethal act that is clearly not an accident so no other intent but suicide can be inferred (e.g. gunshot to head, jumping from window of a high floor/storey). Also, if someone denies intent to die, but they thought that what they did could be lethal, intent maybe inferred. (Have you made a suicide attempt? Have you done anything to harm yourself? Have you done anything dangerous where you could have died? (What did you do? Did you ___ as a way to end your life? Did you want to die (even a little) when you___? Were you trying to end your life when you___? Or did you think it was possible you could have died from___?) Or did you do it purely for other reasons / without ANY intention of killing yourself (like to relieve stress, feel better, get sympathy, or get something else to happen)? (Self-Injurious Behaviour without suicidal intent))

field_name: When the person is interrupted (by an outside circumstance) from starting the potentially self- injurious act (if not for that, actual attempt would have occurred). Shooting: Person has gun pointed towards self, gun is taken away by someone else, or he/she is somehow prevented from pulling trigger. Once they pull the trigger, even if the gun fails to fire, it is an attempt. Jumping: Person is poised to jump, is grabbed and taken down from ledge. Hanging: Person has noose around neck but has not yet started to hang - is stopped from doing so. field_name: Detailed findings of Targeted Neurological Examination
Inclusion 1. Male or NCBP female participants between 18 and 55 years of age, inclusive.
Inclusion 3. In good health as determined by: a) Medical history b) Physical examination c) Neurological examination d) ECG e) Serum chemistry, urinalysis, hematology, and serology tests.

Inclusion 4. Sexually active males who: a) Will commit to utilizing 2 different approved methods of birth control during the trial and for 90 days plus 5 half-lives (ie, 92 days) after the last dose of IMP, or b) Will remain abstinent during the trial and for 90 days plus 5 half-lives (ie, 92 days) after the last dose of IMP. c) Will refrain from sperm donation from the screening visit through 90 days plus 5 half-lives (ie, 92 days) after the last dose of IMP, or d) Have had a bilateral orchiectomy.

Inclusion 5. Female participants who are surgically sterile (ie, have undergone bilateral oophorectomy or hysterectomy) or who have been postmenopausal for at least 12 consecutive months. This will be confirmed with a follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) assessment.

Inclusion 6. Ability to provide written, informed consent prior to initiation of any trial-related procedures, and ability, in the opinion of the principal investigator, to comply with all the requirements of the trial.
Exclusion 1. Non-English speakers and those with language or hearing impairments will not participate in the trial.
Exclusion 2. Participants who are breast-feeding and/or who have a positive pregnancy test result prior to receiving the IMP.

Exclusion 3. Clinically significant abnormality in past medical history, or at the screening physical examination, that in the investigators or sponsor’s opinion may place the participant at risk or interfere with outcome variables including absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drug. This includes, but is not limited to, history of or concurrent cardiac, hepatic, renal, neurologic, endocrine, gastrointestinal, respiratory, hematologic, dermatologic, and immunologic disease.
Exclusion 4. History of drug and/or alcohol abuse within 2 years prior to screening.

Exclusion 5. History of or current hepatitis or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome or carriers of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and/or hepatitis C antibodies (anti-HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibodies. Exceptions are permitted for participants with a prior history of infection with hepatitis A who have fully recovered and are experiencing no liver sequelae, or with hepatitis C who have been adequately treated to be considered cured with no liver sequelae.
Exclusion 6. History of any significant drug allergy or known or suspected hypersensitivity to any component of IMP.
Exclusion 7. A positive urine or breath alcohol test or urine drug screen for substances of abuse at screening or upon check-in to the trial site.
Exclusion 8. Any history of significant bleeding or hemorrhagic tendencies.
Exclusion 9. A history of difficulty in donating blood.
Exclusion 10. The donation of blood or plasma within 30 days prior to the first dose of IMP.
Exclusion 11. Participants having taken an investigational drug within 90 days prior to first dose.

Exclusion 12. Use of prescription, over-the-counter, herbal medications, or vitamin supplements within 14 days prior to the first dose of IMP and oral antibiotics within 30 days prior to the first dose of IMP. The sponsor may allow exceptions only if the medication’s administration is deemed unlikely to impact the PK result.
Exclusion 13. Exposure to any substances known to stimulate hepatic microsomal enzymes within 30 days prior to screening (eg, occupational exposure to pesticides, organic solvents, etc).

Exclusion 14. Use of tobacco products or daily exposure to second-hand smoke within 2 months prior to the screening visit, or urine cotinine concentrations >200 ng/mL or serum cotinine concentrations >20 ng/mL at screening or check-in.

Exclusion 15. Participants presenting with, or having a history of, uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure [SBP] >140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure [DBP] >90 mmHg in the supine position) or symptomatic hypotension or orthostatic hypotension, which is defined as a decrease of ≥20 mmHg in SBP and/or a decrease of ≥10 mmHg in DBP after at least 3 minutes of standing compared with the previous supine blood pressure, at screening or check-in.

Exclusion 18. Abnormal ECG findings at screening or check-in including QT interval corrected for heart rate using Fridericia’s formula (QTcF) >450 msec for male participants or >470 msec for female participants, QRS interval >120 msec, or PR interval >200 msec.
Exclusion 19. Personal or family history of sudden death or long QT syndrome.
Exclusion 20. History of serious mental disorders that, in the opinion of the investigator, would exclude the participant from participating in this trial.
Exclusion 21. Participants with no permanent place of residence.
Exclusion 22. Any participant who, in the opinion of the investigator, should not participate in the trial.

Exclusion 24. Consumption of alcohol and/or food and beverages containing methylxanthines (caffeinated coffee, caffeinated tea, caffeinated soda, and chocolate), pomelo, grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, Seville orange juice, blueberry juice, or cranberry juice within 72 hours prior to dosing.

Exclusion 25. Participants with active suicidal ideation or suicidal behavior within the last 6 months, at the screening visit (Baseline/Screening version), and/or prior to dosing (as evidenced by clinical examination or an answer of “yes” on Questions 4 or 5 of the C SSRS Since Last Visit version) or suicidal behavior is present in the C-SSRS.
Exclusion 26. Not able to consume the FDA HFM (High Fat Meal) for Part 2 and Part 3 within 20 minutes.

Exclusion 27. Participant has any significant primary sleep disorder. Participants with known untreated moderate or severe sleep apnea, other major untreated sleep disorders, or a known diagnosis of a circadian rhythm disorder. Participants adequately treated for obstructive sleep apnea are not excluded.

Exclusion 28. Participants with abnormal liver function and or hepatic impairment, defined as participants with aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), or alkaline phosphatase > the upper limit of normal (ULN) or total bilirubin > the ULN.

field_name: When the person is interrupted (by an outside circumstance) from starting the potentially self- injurious act (if not for that, actual attempt would have occurred). Overdose: Person has pills in hand but is stopped from ingesting. Once they ingest any pills, this becomes an attempt rather than an interrupted attempt. Shooting: Person has gun pointed towards self, gun is taken away by someone else, or he/she is somehow prevented from pulling trigger. Once they pull the trigger, even if the gun fails to fire, it is an attempt. Jumping: Person is poised to jump, is grabbed and taken down from ledge. Hanging: Person has noose around neck but has not yet started to hang - is stopped from doing so. (Has there been a time when you started to do something to end your life but someone or something stopped you before you actually did anything?)

field_name: A potentially self-injurious act committed with at least some wish to die, as a result of act. Behaviour was in part thought of as method to kill oneself. Intent does not have to be 100%. If there is any intent/desire to die associated with the act, then it can be considered an actual suicide attempt. There does not have to be any injury or harm, just the potential for injury or harm. If person pulls trigger while gun is in mouth but gun is broken so no injury results, this is considered an attempt. Inferring Intent: Even if an individual denies intent/wish to die, it may be inferred clinically from the behaviour or circumstances. For example, a highly lethal act that is clearly not an accident so no other intent but suicide can be inferred (e.g. gunshot to head, jumping from window of a high floor/storey). Also, if someone denies intent to die, but they thought that what they did could be lethal, intent maybe inferred. (Have you made a suicide attempt? Have you done anything to harm yourself? Have you done anything dangerous where you could have died? (What did you do? Did you ___ as a way to end your life? Did you want to die (even a little) when you___? Were you trying to end your life when you___? Or did you think it was possible you could have died from___?) Or did you do it purely for other reasons / without ANY intention of killing yourself (like to relieve stress, feel better, get sympathy, or get something else to happen)? (Self-Injurious Behaviour without suicidal intent))
